'''Donald W. Loveland''' (born December 26, 1934)<ref name="profile">Loveland, D.W.; Stickel, M.E.; [http://www.cse.sc.edu/~mgv/csce798F06/GoalTrees.pdf "A Hole in Goal Trees: Some Guidance from Resolution Theory"]. In Proceedings of IEEE Trans. Computers. 1976, 335-341.</ref> is a professor [[emeritus]] of [[computer science]] at [[Duke University]] who specializes in [[artificial intelligence]].<ref name=DU>[http://www.cs.duke.edu/~dwl/ Duke University personal page]</ref> He is well known for the [[Davis–Putnam–Logemann–Loveland algorithm]].<ref>{{cite journal| last=Davis| first=Martin |author2=Logemann, George |author3=Loveland, Donald| title=A Machine Program for Theorem Proving| journal =[[Communications of the ACM]]| volume=5| issue=7| pages = 394–397| year=1962| url=https://archive.org/details/machineprogramfo00davi| doi=10.1145/368273.368557| hdl=2027/mdp.39015095248095| s2cid=15866917 | hdl-access=free}}</ref>

Loveland graduated from [[Oberlin College]] in 1956, received a master's degree from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1958 and a Ph.D. from [[New York University]] in 1964. He joined the Duke University Computer Science Department in 1973. He previously served as a faculty member in the Department of Mathematics at [[New York University]] and [[Carnegie Mellon University]].<ref name="profile"/><ref name=DUCV>[http://www.cs.duke.edu/~dwl/CV/ Curriculum Vitae]</ref><ref name="Duke"/>

He received the [[Herbrand Award]] for Distinguished Contributions to Automated Reasoning in 2001.<ref name="Duke">{{cite web|title=Prestigious Herbrand Award Presented to Duke University Computer Science Faculty Member|url=https://susanalondon.files.wordpress.com/2016/03/press-release.pdf|publisher=Duke University Press Release|access-date=28 August 2016|date=16 July 2001}}</ref> He is a Fellow of the [[Association for Computing Machinery]] (2000),<ref>{{cite web | title=Two Professors Named ACM Fellows | website=Duke University | date=1 November 1999 | url=http://www.cs.duke.edu/news/articles/9 | access-date=28 August 2016 | archive-date=10 October 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161010174442/http://www.cs.duke.edu/news/articles/9 | url-status=dead }}</ref> a Fellow of the [[Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence|Association of Artificial Intelligence]] (1993),<ref>{{cite web | title=Elected AAAI Fellows, Donald W. Loveland, Duke University | website=Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence | url=http://www.aaai.org/Awards/fellows-list.php | quote=For outstanding contributions to the field of automated reasoning and development of the model elimination theorem-proving procedure.| access-date=28 August 2016}}</ref> and a [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (2019).<ref>{{cite journal | title = 2019 AAAS Fellows approved by the AAAS Council| journal = Science| volume = 366| issue = 6469| pages = 1086–1089| date = 29 November 2019| doi = 10.1126/science.366.6469.1086| bibcode = 2019Sci...366.1086.| doi-access = free}}</ref>
